nodes.description: TPIT is required for late differentiation of the POMC lineage but not for lineage commitment. In its absence, presumptive corticotrophs are present at about normal abundance and express early markers such as NeuroD1, but they do not reach terminal differentiation, so the anterior pituitary is left with very few ACTH-producing cells. In the mouse intermediate lobe, cells destined to be melanotrophs instead become gonadotrophs; the human intermediate lobe regresses during fetal life, so this fate switch has no clear human counterpart.

nodes.description: In pituitary POMC-lineage cells TPIT binds a POMC regulatory element next to the homeoprotein PITX1, and the two factors cooperate to activate POMC transcription. TPIT is not expressed in hypothalamic POMC neurons or in other tissues, so its loss removes POMC expression specifically from the pituitary while sparing extra-pituitary POMC.

nodes.description: Biallelic germline TBX19 variants abolish the function of the T-box transcription factor TPIT. Reported alleles include nonsense and frameshift variants that trigger nonsense-mediated mRNA decay, splice-site and exonic synonymous variants that cause missplicing, multi-exon deletions, and missense variants within the T-box that abolish DNA binding or disrupt protein-protein interactions with PITX1 and coactivators.
